3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The thrum of helicopter blades was almost deafening as we prepared for our descent into the Meftiem International Trade Zone.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: I looked out the window. We were above the Meftiem Basin, an expansive dried-up lake containing millions of years' worth of sedimentary deposits.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Smoke rose from the surrounding refineries, turning the sky a musty shade of orange.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: We gently touched down on the helipad of the Cooperation Center, the building where MITZ board meetings and other diplomatic functions were held.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: My eyes followed a cargo-laden freight train as it departed the Meftiem station. Next to me in the helicopter, Elena noticed it as well.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: We were immediately met by a large security retinue and ushered inside to the reception hall, where the welcome ceremony was to take place.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Alma Saltana greeted us by the entrance. A security staff member showed Elena to her seat, while I followed the Morellan prime minister to the front of the hall.

10.speaker: Elena Werner
10.text: "One of Lespia's, by the looks of it. The gold will be shipped out of the Muardien Port and reach Veno Robin by this evening."

11.speaker: Player_Romus
11.text: "Lespia, eh? I hope Prime Minister Alvarez remembers I took his side at the AN."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "A Lespian train? Do you think I can spit on it from here?"

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "Lespia doesn't need gold. Not now that it's about to have Palesian gas."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "And from there, straight into Prime Minister Alvarez's pocket."

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "The birthplace of Lespian Protectionism, relying on international partnerships for gold imports. Tell me how that squares up."

22.speaker: Elena Werner
22.text: "I'm sure he hasn't forgotten. But he will be expecting you to follow up on your words with action today."

24.speaker: Elena Werner
24.text: "With one or two detours in between. But yes, Alvarez has no small personal stake in the operations here."

25.speaker: Elena Werner
25.text: "You're absolutely right, Your Majesty. Lespian economic theory does favor domestic production over foreign imports."

26.speaker: Elena Werner
26.text: "Our northern neighbors have a certain standard of wealth to uphold. Especially as an ATO member."

27.speaker: Elena Werner
27.text: "Are you ready for today's meeting? I know neither of us wants Morella's nationalization plans to succeed."

31.speaker: Elena Werner
31.text: "I recall you took a rather pro-Morella stance at the Alliance of Nations session. Are you still leaning in that direction?"

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "You shall address me as 'Your Majesty', Madam Prime Minister."

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "Of course, Comrade Saltana. I'm grateful for the chance to speak with you."

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "Prime Minister Saltana. A pleasure to see you again."

38.speaker: Alma Saltana
38.text: "Excuse me, Your Majesty. We're no longer used to such titles in this country."

39.speaker: Alma Saltana
39.text: "I was gladdened to hear you were able to reach an understanding with Wehlen. It gives me hope for today's talks."

41.speaker: Alma Saltana
41.text: "And you. I hope you've been well since our encounter at the AN."

46.speaker: Alma Saltana
46.text: "I'll assume that is not an attempt to mock me."

47.speaker: Alma Saltana
47.text: "I'd like to start straight away, but my advisors have persuaded me that diplomatic protocol must be followed."

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: She gestured for me to follow her.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: A stage had been set up backdropped by our countries' four flags. Patricio Alvarez was already sitting there, looking somewhat bored.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: I took my place next to him. He didn't acknowledge me.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I took my place next to him. He gave me a nod of acknowledgement.
52.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true  or  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == false)) == false

55.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
55.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Morella_ANSpeech_SideWith"] == true  or  (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Cede"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == false)) == false

62.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
62.text: "It had better be a good afternoon, Your Majesty."

64.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
64.text: "It was fine, Your Majesty. Thank you."

66.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
66.text: "Not bad. We had to take a motorcade from Stadelle. Can you believe there's nowhere to land a private jet around here?"

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: The doors to the hall suddenly swung open. Emmerich Hegel entered, accompanied by a pair of bodyguards.

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: The hall began to fill up with dignitaries, ministers and heads of corporations.

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: Alvarez glanced around, then reached into his pocket and pulled out a flask. He took a furtive sip and offered it to me.

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "I don't drink. I thought you didn't either."

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: I noticed a certain bleariness in his eyes. I wondered whether his decision to quit drinking had lasted.

79.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
79.text: "We've got a long meeting ahead of us. Got to take the edge off somehow."

80.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
80.text: "The stress of this job gets to a man. I'm impressed you've managed to hold out."

81.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
81.text: "Yes, well, the stress of this job gets to a man. There was only so long I could hold out."

82.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
82.text: "They don't understand the stress of this job. Hardly anyone does."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "I'll leave you to it. I'd rather stay sharp for today's meeting."

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: He stuffed the flask back into his pocket as the hall began to fill with dignitaries, ministers and executives.

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: He passed me the flask and I took a quick sip. He stuffed it back in his pocket as the hall began to fill with dignitaries, ministers and executives.

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: He gave me a reproachful look as he stuffed the flask back in his pocket. The hall began to fill with dignitaries, ministers and executives.

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: Rusty Montoro was in the back row, talking animatedly to a Lespian politician. He didn't so much as glance in my direction.

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Rusty Montoro was in the back row, talking animatedly to a Lespian politician. He broke off his conversation to throw me a smile.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: He and Prime Minister Saltana exchanged cheek kisses. Alvarez could barely disguise his look of scorn.

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: Saltana and Hegel joined us on stage. The Valgslandian chancellor shook my hand with an enigmatic smile.

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: Saltana and Hegel joined us on stage. The Valgslandian chancellor shook my hand with an encouraging smile.

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: Saltana and Hegel joined us on stage. The Valgslandian chancellor frowned sternly as he shook my hand.

103.speaker: Narrator
103.text: The four of us posed for photographs. The Morellan national anthem was played, then those of Valgsland, Rizia and finally Lespia.

104.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
104.text: "Hmm. That shows who takes what priority, doesn't it?"

105.speaker: Player_Romus
105.text: "Good to see you, Chancellor. Actually, I was hoping we could speak in private later."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "Good that you made it. It's time we settled this silly debate."

109.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
109.text: "It is not silly, Mr. Toras. Lives and livelihoods rest on our decisions today."

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: When the music died down, we were escorted to a conference room together with our key ministers, security detail and a number of legal advisors.

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Once we were seated, Prime Minister Saltana spoke.

112.speaker: Alma Saltana
112.text: "Thank you for carving time out of your schedules to join me today, gentlemen."

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: She looked around the table at each of us.

114.speaker: Alma Saltana
114.text: "Over 35 years ago, our countries signed an agreement regarding the sharing of resources in the Meftiem basin."

115.speaker: Alma Saltana
115.text: "At that time, Morella was capable neither of exploring the full potential of the gold located here, nor of fending off raids from our Derdian neighbors."

116.speaker: Alma Saltana
116.text: "It was only with the cooperation of Rizia, Valgsland and Lespia that the Meftiem International Trade Zone could become the thriving industrial center it is today."

117.speaker: Alma Saltana
117.text: "However, our predecessors failed to recognize the social and moral responsibility that comes with such an economic endeavor. And Morella paid the price."

119.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
119.text: "Oh, just the chance to make history today."

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "I still want to know why Valgsland is only supporting nationalization now. Why didn't you hand your ITZ stake back to Morella right after the revolution?"

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "As a supporter of the 'Save the Arufelde' initiative, I want to know how your nationalization plan will tackle the pollution issue."

124.speaker: Alma Saltana
124.text: "Toxic chemicals continue to leach into the river's watershed, and are slowly poisoning the surrounding communities."

125.speaker: Alma Saltana
125.text: "I might add that the river empties into the gulf of Moridia, which is bordered by Rizia, Derdia and Wehlen as well as my country."

138.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
138.text: "The CSP has no involvement in what is happening here. Ms. Saltana is merely standing up for the rights of her own countrymen and women."

139.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
139.text: "Is she? Then let me hear it from her own mouth. Ms. Saltana, can you confirm you have no interest in joining the Contanan Security Pact?"

140.speaker: Alma Saltana
140.text: "Our struggle for control of the MITZ is connected with the worldwide struggle against a system that prioritizes capital gains over human welfare. That's all I will say."

144.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
144.text: "Well, Lespia stands firm in our conviction that the ownership of the MITZ should not change."

148.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
148.text: "And I suspect His Majesty King Romus feels the same way."

149.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
149.text: "If His Majesty knows what's good for his kingdom, he'll agree with me."

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Everyone seated at the table turned to look at me. Elena cleared her throat.

151.speaker: Elena Werner
151.text: "Are you ready for the vote, Your Majesty?"

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "No, I have a few more questions for the board."

157.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
157.text: "You're still on the fence? I remember you made your position very clear to me."

158.speaker: Alma Saltana
158.text: "I don't wish you to take this decision lightly, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. What else do you want to know?"

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "Actually, Ms. Werner, I would like to confer with you privately before making my final decision."

165.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
165.text: "You're still on the fence? I remember you made your position very clear to me."

166.speaker: Alma Saltana
166.text: "Absolutely, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. Take all the time you need."

173.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
173.text: "I would just like to point out what a towering achievement it is that the MITZ exists in the first place."

174.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
174.text: "Four countries with four vastly different governments, coming together for the economic benefit of all? It sounds preposterous, yet it works."

175.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
175.text: "The cooperation -- and yes, competition -- involved in sharing this valuable resource has not only brought our nations closer together, it's spurred innovation far beyond what any of us could achieve individually."

176.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
176.text: "We could harness that same spirit to address the very valid concerns Ms. Saltana has brought up about the environment and human rights."

178.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
178.text: "Or we could throw all of that away, scare off investors and put God knows how many people out of work, because... why exactly? To score a few points with our eastern comrades?"

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: Saltana and Hegel both had icy stares on their faces.

181.speaker: Alma Saltana
181.text: "In the case of a split decision, we would have to renegotiate the initial MITZ agreement until a way forward is found."

182.speaker: Alma Saltana
182.text: "But Morella will no longer accept the status quo."

184.speaker: Player_Romus
184.text: "As the King of Rizia, I vote in favor of nationalization. The International Trade Zone should be under Morellan ownership."

185.speaker: Player_Romus
185.text: "I vote against nationalization. However, I am open to renegotiating our original agreement to recognize the contributions and sacrifices made by the nation of Morella."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "The International Trade Zone should not be nationalized. Furthermore, I do not believe our resource and profit sharing agreement should be changed in any way."

188.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
188.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ArgumentAgainst"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Violations"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Advantages"]== true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ValgslandReparations"] == true

189.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
189.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ArgumentAgainst"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Violations"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Advantages"]== true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ValgslandReparations"] == true) == false

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "All right. I'm ready to move forward with my decision."
190.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ArgumentAgainst"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Violations"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_Advantages"]== true  or  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZNationalization_ValgslandReparations"] == true

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "I would still like to confer with my treasurer before casting my official vote."

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Alvarez sighed audibly. Prime Minister Saltana nodded.

202.speaker: Narrator
202.text: The others at the table glanced around impatiently. Prime Minister Saltana nodded.

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: The group dispersed. Elena and I were seated in a smaller private conference room.

205.speaker: Alma Saltana
205.text: "We'll set up a separate room for you. The rest of us can break for coffee."

206.speaker: Player_Romus
206.text: "Of course. He owns the majority of Rizian Royal Gold, after all."

208.speaker: Elena Werner
208.text: "I do think Mr. Montoro should be privy to this conversation as well."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "I don't see why. The Rizian government is the primary operator in the MITZ, not him."

210.speaker: Player_Romus
210.text: "Yes, good idea. This decision does greatly affect his company."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "I don't see the need. Don't we already know what he's going to say?"

212.speaker: Elena Werner
212.text: "Well, yes. But he certainly wouldn't appreciate being left out of this discussion."

213.speaker: Elena Werner
213.text: "Well, yes, but we operate using equipment and contractors from RRG. Nationalization would affect them greatly."

214.speaker: Elena Werner
214.text: "We do operate our part of the MITZ using equipment and contractors from Rizian Royal Gold, after all."

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "We can talk to him later. For now, I don't want him influencing my decision."

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: Elena notified an aide to send for Rusty. A few minutes later, he appeared.

219.speaker: Elena Werner
219.text: "Very well. I suspect we'll be hearing from him about this."

220.speaker: Russello Montoro
220.text: "Your Majesty. Elena. Have you tried Morellan sukhar biscuits yet? They're drier than a letter from my ex-wife's divorce attorney."

221.speaker: Russello Montoro
221.text: "We are here to talk about biscuits, aren't we? Because as far as I'm concerned, the nationalization debate doesn't merit a discussion."

223.speaker: Elena Werner
223.text: "King Romus here is the leader of our country. If he says a discussion is necessary, then it is."

224.speaker: Russello Montoro
224.text: "Oh. My sincerest apologies to you both. I was just joking."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "I don't like the idea of nationalization either. But I want my decision to be fully informed."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "Well, I am not laughing. Consider yourself lucky to even be in this room right now."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "You're right, though. Those biscuits are drier than Ms. Werner's financial reports."

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: Rusty let out a laugh. Elena clicked her tongue disapprovingly.

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: Elena nodded in agreement, then glanced up at the clock.

230.speaker: Elena Werner
230.text: "We don't have long. Where would you like to begin, Your Majesty."

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "What will be the economic and financial impact on Rizia if Morella goes through with the nationalization plan?"

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "What was Rizian Royal Gold's role in the labor and environmental violations that have occurred in the MITZ?"

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "Is there any scenario where we can *increase* our MITZ stake? Say, by renegotiating the profit sharing agreement in our favor?"

236.speaker: Elena Werner
236.text: "But by privately negotiating the proposal terms with Prime Minister Saltana, we may yet be able to make an arrangement where we come out relatively unscathed."

237.speaker: Elena Werner
237.text: "That depends on the exact nature of the agreement, doesn't it?"

238.speaker: Russello Montoro
238.text: "That'd be a real risk, Your Majesty. RRG already almost went belly-up after we lost Zille."

242.speaker: Elena Werner
242.text: "If we cannot do that, we run the risk of losing a significant income source."

246.speaker: Russello Montoro
246.text: "Add to that the cost of implementing those new regulations you ordered and, well, nationalization could be a killing blow."

247.speaker: Elena Werner
247.text: "And the new regulations you ordered were quite costly to implement, though I remain convinced they were worth it."

251.speaker: Elena Werner
251.text: "At the same time, we are facing high gold demand from Rumburg and, soon, Wehlen."

255.speaker: Elena Werner
255.text: "At the same time, we are facing the usual high gold demand from Rumburg."

256.speaker: Elena Werner
256.text: "We have our new gas holdings to fall back on, as long as Duke Reinhart does not renege on his end of the agreement."

260.speaker: Elena Werner
260.text: "With little in the way of gas holdings, it would be difficult for Rizia to carry on as a resource-based economy."
260.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true) == false)

261.speaker: Russello Montoro
261.text: "Thanks to you, we didn't have to waste money on needless safely regulations. But still, nationalization could be a killing blow."

262.speaker: Elena Werner
262.text: "Your rejection of the RPP's safety proposal helped keep the status quo, but nationalization would definitely be a big blow."

263.speaker: Player_Romus
263.text: "I see. Good that we have the gas as a safety net."

264.speaker: Player_Romus
264.text: "I didn't know the situation was this grave."

265.speaker: Player_Romus
265.text: "Maybe that's for the best. Both of those resources would deplete eventually anyway."

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "It won't come to that. We're keeping our gold share no matter what."

267.speaker: Elena Werner
267.text: "The agreement is still being deliberated on. We really should solidify it."

268.speaker: Elena Werner
268.text: "It's not grave yet. But we should refrain from making rash promises."

269.speaker: Elena Werner
269.text: "If that's your primary goal, then we shouldn't vote for nationalization."

270.speaker: Elena Werner
270.text: "Yes, I have always thought it wise not to rely so much on either."

274.speaker: Elena Werner
274.text: "We have our new gas holdings to fall back on, as long as Mr. Alvarez does not renege on his end of the agreement."
274.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Lespia_GasField_25PercentDeal"] == true)

275.speaker: Elena Werner
275.text: "Such a scenario isn't impossible, but it will be difficult."

279.speaker: Russello Montoro
279.text: "Ha! I like the way you're thinking."

280.speaker: Elena Werner
280.text: "Morella will demand a larger profit share if the board votes against nationalization. Not without reason."

281.speaker: Elena Werner
281.text: "With Hegel and Saltana presenting a united front, it will likely come down to Rizia versus Lespia."

283.speaker: Player_Romus
283.text: "It's a zero-sum game. Morella's stake can't grow unless one of ours shrinks."

284.speaker: Elena Werner
284.text: "Or you present Morella with something better than a larger stake."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "At least Saltana seems to hate Alvarez."

286.speaker: Elena Werner
286.text: "Don't underestimate Lespia's wealth. If the Prime Minister presents a good enough deal, hate will fall by the wayside."

290.speaker: Elena Werner
290.text: "That would be in line with your intention to position Rizia closer to ATO."

294.speaker: Elena Werner
294.text: "That would put us further from our goal of improving relations with our non-ATO neighbors."

295.speaker: Elena Werner
295.text: "At the expense of our relations with Morella, of course."

296.speaker: Elena Werner
296.text: "In addition to the MITZ, Morella and Rizia share a long border. I would prefer we find a compromise to preserve our relations with our neighbor."

297.speaker: Elena Werner
297.text: "I am all for finding a compromise in order to preserve our relations with our neighbor."

298.speaker: Elena Werner
298.text: "The question is whether we will be able to offer Morella something that Lespia cannot."

313.speaker: Russello Montoro
313.text: "First of all, I will remind you that Rizian Royal Gold never made our own decisions in the MITZ. We only acted on behalf of whoever wore the crown."

314.speaker: Russello Montoro
314.text: "All we ever did was follow the rules. What incentive would we possibly have had for going above and beyond?"

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "So the Rizian government engaged in worker exploitation and toxic waste dumping simply because it was allowed to."

316.speaker: Russello Montoro
316.text: "Because Lespia and Morella were doing it too. And Valgsland, for many more years than Comrade Hegel is willing to admit."

317.speaker: Russello Montoro
317.text: "Might I remind you that if Rizia hadn't been able to keep our gold prices competitive, Rumburg would never have reached out to us about an alliance."

318.speaker: Russello Montoro
318.text: "What I mean to say is, you're welcome, Your Majesty."

320.speaker: Player_Romus
320.text: "Ms. Werner, you advised my father. Did you never once speak to him about this?"

321.speaker: Player_Romus
321.text: "I am sorry for what your people have gone through."

322.speaker: Player_Romus
322.text: "Any plan, for nationalization or otherwise, must address this."

324.speaker: Alma Saltana
324.text: "The time for apologies is long past, Your Majesty. The time for action has arrived."

325.speaker: Player_Romus
325.text: "But who allowed for the runoff to happen in the first place, Ms. Saltana? The board could have implemented better regulations from the start."

326.speaker: Player_Romus
326.text: "How do you know the damage you speak of is tied to the mines? Anything could have contaminated that river."

328.speaker: Elena Werner
328.text: "In the meantime, what did you still want to know regarding the nationalization debate?"

330.speaker: Elena Werner
330.text: "Technically speaking, Your Majesty, there were no violations. RRG acted according to the regulations agreed on by all four MITZ partners."

331.speaker: Elena Werner
331.text: "Furthermore, they're merely contractors here. They've been acting on behalf of the Crown this entire time."

333.speaker: Elena Werner
333.text: "It was a hard time for Rizia's economy. We were under pressure to keep gold prices competitive, especially after the uprising."

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "In other words, if more stringent regulations were placed on the MITZ, RRG would follow those?"

335.speaker: Russello Montoro
335.text: "The economy never would've recovered from '26, the populace would still be sore at the monarchy and the dearly departed Princess Lena would never have laid a hand on your royal scepter."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "Don't worry. I am not blaming you."

337.speaker: Elena Werner
337.text: "For Dast's sake, Rusty, be more respectful to your king."

338.speaker: Elena Werner
338.text: "Prime Minister Saltana's predecessors agreed to keep regulations lax in the MITZ to attract investment. All four partners took advantage of that, Morella and Valgsland included."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "Ms. Werner, you advised my father. Did you never once speak to him about this?"

342.speaker: Elena Werner
342.text: "It was a hard time for Rizia's economy. We were under pressure to keep gold prices low, especially after the uprising."

343.speaker: Elena Werner
343.text: "Prime Minister Saltana's predecessors agreed to keep regulations lax in the MITZ to attract investment. All four partners took advantage of that, Morella and Valgsland included."

345.speaker: Elena Werner
345.text: "We'd have to secure compliance from all four partners. Otherwise, one of them -- say, Lespia -- might gain an unfair advantage."

346.speaker: Player_Romus
346.text: "So the Rizian government engaged in worker exploitation and toxic waste dumping simply because they were allowed to."

347.speaker: Elena Werner
347.text: "Because everyone else was doing the same. Including Morella and Valgsland."

348.speaker: Elena Werner
348.text: "If your father's regime had voluntarily cracked down on those practices, our gold prices would have skyrocketed. The Rumburg alliance would be nothing more than a pipe dream."

353.speaker: Player_Romus
353.text: "It makes me sick that my own house was complicit in this."

354.speaker: Alma Saltana
354.text: "My predecessors intentionally kept ITZ regulations lax to attract investment. They were willing to overlook the consequences as long as they kept turning a profit."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "But you would not be willing to decrease Lespia's profit share."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "You are doing Morella a disservice by resorting to such a gross oversimplification."

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "A nice thought. But I have a hunch that as long as Lespia keeps its stake in the MITZ, sustainability will always come second to profit."

360.speaker: Player_Romus
360.text: "You see, Mr. Hegel and Ms. Saltana? Ideological differences shouldn't keep us from preserving what we've created."

361.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
361.text: "Exactly. All of us care about improving conditions here."

362.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
362.text: "Why are you pointing the finger at Lespia? Our share is no larger than yours."

363.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
363.text: "But not an inaccurate one, right, Your Majesty?"

364.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
364.text: "I am willing to dedicate time and resources to improve conditions in the MITZ. Isn't that enough?"

365.speaker: Alma Saltana
365.text: "Was your donation a mere token gesture, then?"

366.speaker: Alma Saltana
366.text: "For your information, the sulphate and heavy metal levels found in the river could only be a result of mining."

370.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
370.text: "Mr. Toras, if you meant what you said at the AN, you shouldn't even be entertaining this opinion."

372.speaker: Alma Saltana
372.text: "Whatever is decided today, I am willing to work with both Rizia and Lespia. Our differing outlooks shouldn't get in the way of a peaceful compromise."

374.speaker: Narrator
374.text: The past decades of industrial activity had turned it into a mosaic of underground and open-pit mines linked by roads, railways and makeshift canals.

378.speaker: Narrator
378.text: I turned to look at Alvarez. His eyes were shooting daggers into me.

380.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
380.text: "A wise choice, Mr. Toras. History will reward you for it."

381.speaker: Alma Saltana
381.text: "I am as surprised as I am grateful, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. I look forward to collaborating with you on a fair proposal."

383.speaker: Narrator
383.text: I turned to look at Alvarez. He had an artificial smile on his face.

384.speaker: Narrator
384.text: He looked at the other two leaders at the table.

385.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
385.text: "Let the record show that the King of Rizia cannot be trusted to keep a promise."

387.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
387.text: "You can count on my cooperation. I am absolutely brimming with suggestions."

396.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
396.text: "So your words at the AN were merely for show."

397.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
397.text: "I did not expect anything else from you, Mr. Toras."

401.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
401.text: "Fortunately, there are some in your country who have compassion for the downtrodden. And there will be more."

402.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
402.text: "A monarch will never have compassion for the downtrodden. It's not in his nature."

403.speaker: Alma Saltana
403.text: "Take heart, Comrade Hegel. If the King of Rizia is truly willing to build a fairer and more sustainable ITZ with us, then today was not a total loss."

407.speaker: Alma Saltana
407.text: "Take heart, Comrade Hegel. I'm sure that both Rizia and Lespia will join us at the negotiating table in due time."

408.speaker: Narrator
408.text: I turned to look at Alvarez. He had a plastic smile on his face.

409.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
409.text: "Yes, I too am willing to work on a new ITZ agreement that takes into account the complaints Prime Minister Saltana has made today."

410.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
410.text: "We can all be proud of what we have accomplished in this room today."

411.speaker: Narrator
411.text: I turned to look at Alvarez. He had a plastic smile on his face.

412.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
412.text: "I am with King Romus. We will build a more equitable ITZ through friendly cooperation, not profit-snatching."

413.speaker: Player_Romus
413.text: "That's to be expected. I understand completely."

414.speaker: Elena Werner
414.text: "Or nudged into compliance by governments and shareholders."

415.speaker: Elena Werner
415.text: "If that had not been the case, your father would have been deposed. Or worse."

419.speaker: Player_Romus
419.text: "We forced corporations to treat their workers better in Rizia. We can do the same here."

420.speaker: Elena Werner
420.text: "The MITZ is a much more complicated ecosystem, Your Majesty. But yes, it should be possible."

421.speaker: Elena Werner
421.text: "I wouldn't call it greed, Your Majesty. More like survival."

422.speaker: Player_Romus
422.text: "But if more stringent regulations were placed on the MITZ, your company would follow those?"

424.speaker: Russello Montoro
424.text: "Of course, the other MITZ partners would have to agree to the same thing. We can't have one of them gaining an unfair advantage over us."

425.speaker: Russello Montoro
425.text: "Think about it, Your Majesty. If it hadn't been for the MITZ, the economy never would've recovered from '26, the populace would still be sore at the monarchy and the dearly departed Princess Lena would never have laid a hand on your royal scepter."

429.speaker: Player_Romus
429.text: "I recall you made the same case against safety regulations in Rizia. I didn't buy it then, and I don't now."

430.speaker: Russello Montoro
430.text: "Oh, we did lose a pretty penny from those regulations. But we just about balanced it out with royalties from the mines here. If we lose that, well... don't blame me."

431.speaker: Player_Romus
431.text: "My councilor is right. The Crown's debts to RRG do not give you license to besmirch the memory of my wife. Apologize now."

432.speaker: Narrator
432.text: Rusty's face assumed an abashed expression.

433.speaker: Russello Montoro
433.text: "Truly sorry, Your Majesty. No more besmirching."

434.speaker: Player_Romus
434.text: "My father made the right decision at the time. But something has to change."

435.speaker: Elena Werner
435.text: "I agree. And this is an opportunity to change four countries' policies in one."

436.speaker: Narrator
436.text: Saltana looked puzzled for a moment, but shook it off.

438.speaker: Alma Saltana
438.text: "We should inform our guests of the good news. Let's get back to the reception hall."

441.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
441.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_Damage"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_Negotiation"] == false  and  Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_RRGViolation"] == false) == false

442.speaker: Player_Romus
442.text: "No questions, really. I just wanted to keep everyone out there waiting a bit longer."

450.speaker: Elena Werner
450.text: "I think we've made our point. Let's reconvene with the others."

456.speaker: Russello Montoro
456.text: "You know what to do, Your Majesty."

460.speaker: Russello Montoro
460.text: "Good luck with the vote, Your Majesty."

464.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
464.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_Damage"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_Negotiation"] == true  or Variable["RiziaDLCIsolated.Turn05_ITZEconQs_RRGViolation"] == true) == false

465.speaker: Player_Romus
465.text: "That was everything I wanted to talk about."

469.speaker: Russello Montoro
469.text: "You're sure about that, Your Majesty? I'm very happy to talk more about the long-term negative impact of nationalization."

471.speaker: Elena Werner
471.text: "Very good, Your Majesty. Let's reconvene with the others."

473.speaker: Elena Werner
473.text: "No, we've taken enough time here. We should reconvene with the others."

474.speaker: Narrator
474.text: He motioned for the guards to escort him out to the reception hall.

475.speaker: Narrator
475.text: We headed back to the conference room and settled back into our seats.

476.speaker: Player_Romus
476.text: "I am ready to proceed with the vote."

479.speaker: Player_Romus
479.text: "Actually, *now* I have a few questions for the board."

480.speaker: Narrator
480.text: Alvarez quietly groaned in frustration. Saltana bowed her head.

483.speaker: Narrator
483.text: Saltana rose from her seat energetically.

484.speaker: Narrator
484.text: The Rizian, Valgslandian and Lespian delegations slowly began filing out of the conference room. Next to me, Elena spoke under her breath.

485.speaker: Narrator
485.text: As Alvarez and I stood up, I saw him take another sip from his flask. He noticed my gaze and nodded slightly.

486.speaker: Alma Saltana
486.text: "We should inform our guests of the decision. Let's get back to the reception hall."

487.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
487.text: "So it's you and me against the Malenyevists."

488.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
488.text: "So you sided with the Malenyevists in the end."

489.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
489.text: "So we're making deals with the Malenyevists now."

490.speaker: Narrator
490.text: He stepped past me and out the door.

491.speaker: Narrator
491.text: We hit a rough patch of air as we continued our descent. I felt the gold disc in my suit pocket bump against my side.

498.speaker: Player_Romus
498.text: "By the way, didn't you mention back in Qalus that you were an expert on antique coins?"

500.speaker: Narrator
500.text: Rusty had mentioned that it had been found here in the MITZ. I wondered what its significance was.

501.speaker: Elena Werner
501.text: "Why, yes. You remember more about that night than I do, Your Majesty."

502.speaker: Narrator
502.text: She adjusted her hair with a proud smile.

503.speaker: Narrator
503.text: I showed her the disc Rusty had given me. Her eyes widened in glee.

504.speaker: Elena Werner
504.text: "That's no coin, Your Majesty. It's a Rezenid-era Wruhecist prayer medallion."

505.speaker: Elena Werner
505.text: "It was originally worn around one's neck, with the intention of keeping St. Wruhec's teachings close to your heart at all times."

506.speaker: Player_Romus
506.text: "Sounds like it could also be helpful in warding off an assassination attempt."

507.speaker: Player_Romus
507.text: "How much do you think it's worth?"

508.speaker: Player_Romus
508.text: "I see. More proof that the Lord has chosen me to rule."

509.speaker: Elena Werner
509.text: "I wouldn't rely on an assassin to be such a good marksman to hit that thing."

510.speaker: Elena Werner
510.text: "It could be thousands. It's very old and very rare."

511.speaker: Elena Werner
511.text: "One could see it that way, Your Majesty."

515.speaker: Player_Romus
515.text: "Who'd wear one of these when they could spend it?"

516.speaker: Elena Werner
516.text: "There are things more valuable than gold. Not many, but a few."

520.speaker: Player_Romus
520.text: "Sorry to leave you in the lurch, Mr. Prime Minister."

521.speaker: Player_Romus
521.text: "I did. Do you have a problem with it?"

522.speaker: Player_Romus
522.text: "Are you surprised? I made my intentions clear."

526.speaker: Player_Romus
526.text: "I didn't vote for nationalization. I held up my end of our bargain."

531.speaker: Player_Romus
531.text: "I held up my end of the bargain, didn't I?"

535.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
535.text: "You did, Your Majesty. But the real bargaining hasn't even started yet."

536.speaker: Player_Romus
536.text: "I'm telling you, I will not give up a single cent."

537.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
537.text: "Nor will I, Your Majesty. Safety in numbers."

538.speaker: Player_Romus
538.text: "It's the only way forward that benefits everyone."

540.speaker: Player_Romus
540.text: "This isn't just a fight for the MITZ. It's a fight against the forces of evil."

544.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
544.text: "A little melodramatic, Your Majesty. But rest assured good will triumph."

545.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
545.text: "I'll tell you right away that I don't intend to lose a damn cent."

546.speaker: Player_Romus
546.text: "No, we're not. I just told Hegel and his puppet what they wanted to hear."

548.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
548.text: "Because I'll tell you right away that I don't intend to lose a damn cent."

549.speaker: Player_Romus
549.text: "Their ideology doesn't have anything to do with it. I just want to keep my money."

551.speaker: Elena Werner
551.text: "But they make an exception for resources like gold and gas, especially when Lespian companies have a hand in their extraction."

552.speaker: Player_Romus
552.text: "Of course I am. Do you accuse the King of Rizia of waffling?"

553.speaker: Player_Romus
553.text: "Yes. The Trade Zone is on Morellan land, so naturally Morella should have a greater say in its operations."

554.speaker: Player_Romus
554.text: "I want to respect Morella's wishes. But we can't ignore the MITZ's great economic importance to our kingdom."

555.speaker: Player_Romus
555.text: "No, not since my talk with President Smolak. We cannot afford to lose any more of our gold."

556.speaker: Player_Romus
556.text: "Do not assume that, Ms. Werner. I am approaching the talks with an open mind."

557.speaker: Player_Romus
557.text: "Morella's wishes carry weight. But we can't ignore the MITZ's great importance to our kingdom."

558.speaker: Player_Romus
558.text: "Indeed not. I am not about to let the Malenyevists steamroll over our economic interests."

562.speaker: Player_Romus
562.text: "An understatement, Ms. Werner. My recent talk with President Smolak made it clear that we must protect our remaining gold reserves at all costs."

563.speaker: Elena Werner
563.text: "No, we can't. I'm sure we can reach a compromise that doesn't result in a total loss for us."

564.speaker: Elena Werner
564.text: "Perhaps so, Your Majesty. At the same time, we cannot simply hand over our assets to Morella without suffering serious economic consequences."

565.speaker: Elena Werner
565.text: "No, Your Majesty. Your resolve is unmatched."

566.speaker: Elena Werner
566.text: "You're absolutely right. But we also can't completely ignore Morella's demands."

567.speaker: Elena Werner
567.text: "Of course, Your Majesty. No decision should be made without listening to all sides."

568.speaker: Elena Werner
568.text: "Agreed. As valid as Morella's concerns may be, their new ideology should not get in the way of our business agreement."

569.speaker: Elena Werner
569.text: "We should listen to Morella's concerns, of course. But no, we cannot simply hand over our assets on a platter."

576.speaker: Alma Saltana
576.text: "I was sorry to hear you were unable to reach an agreement with Wehlen. I'm confident today's talks will go more smoothly."

580.speaker: Player_Romus
580.text: "If you are as open to negotiation as President Smolak was, I don't foresee a problem."

581.speaker: Player_Romus
581.text: "We haven't solidified our agreement yet. In fact, it would be very helpful to have the international community on our side right now."

584.speaker: Player_Romus
584.text: "Thank you, Prime Minister Saltana. The support of the international community means a lot to us at this time."

585.speaker: Player_Romus
585.text: "As you see, my kingdom is not desperate. I will reject any so-called solution that does not benefit the Rizian people."

586.speaker: Alma Saltana
586.text: "I hope you'll understand that I am not able to offer my public support. Not yet, at least."

588.speaker: Player_Romus
588.text: "It was a different circumstance, Ms. Saltana. I plan to drive a much harder bargain today."

589.speaker: Player_Romus
589.text: "I would not call it an 'understanding'. Wehlen is holding our land hostage."

590.speaker: Alma Saltana
590.text: "Given the violent history of our region, any solution that doesn't involve bloodshed should be regarded as a success, wouldn't you say?"

595.speaker: Alma Saltana
595.text: "I understand. I feel the same about my republic."

596.speaker: Player_Romus
596.text: "I'm sure they will. You are nowhere near as noxious a negotiating partner as President Smolak."

597.speaker: Alma Saltana
597.text: "I understand. I feel the same about my republic."

601.speaker: Player_Romus
601.text: "Yes, I'm sure you're disappointed that I didn't kowtow to your communist crony."

602.speaker: Alma Saltana
602.text: "We do share certain anti-imperialist sentiments, but President Smolak is not my 'crony'."

603.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
603.text: "It's just a ceremony, Mr. Alvarez. Don't read too much into it."

605.speaker: Player_Romus
605.text: "If the MITZ has truly had such a negative effect on Morella, why has no other leader before you brought this up?"

606.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
606.text: "There is only one way forward. The MITZ must be restored to Morellan ownership."

607.speaker: Player_Romus
607.text: "I beg to differ, Ms. Saltana. Whether at home or abroad, the Kingdom of Rizia has always been committed to responsible mining practices."

608.speaker: Player_Romus
608.text: "It is high time for us to revisit the original agreement."

609.speaker: Alma Saltana
609.text: "I am afraid my government will not be satisfied with cosmetic adjustments to the MITZ contract."

613.speaker: Alma Saltana
613.text: "I appreciate the recent laws that you have passed in Rizia. However, they do not make up for the damage that has been done here."

614.speaker: Alma Saltana
614.text: "I wish I could believe that. But your failure to pass even basic mining safety legislature in Rizia speaks volumes."

615.speaker: Alma Saltana
615.text: "Morella's previous governments were content to focus on the profits that could be squeezed out of the MITZ, not the consequences. But my coalition's rise to power shows how priorities have changed."

617.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
617.text: "Is this actually what you believe, *Miss* Saltana? Or are you just parroting the words of Chancellor Hegel?"

618.speaker: Player_Romus
618.text: "Please calm down, Mr. Alvarez. You may disagree with the Morellan prime minister, but that doesn't give you an excuse to belittle her."

620.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
620.text: "You're right, of course. But my question still stands."

621.speaker: Player_Romus
621.text: "That isn't the way I would have phrased it, but I too have concerns about the growing closeness between Morella and the Republic of Valgsland."

622.speaker: Player_Romus
622.text: "Clearly it is the latter. Only a Valgslandian socialist would believe nationalization is a better choice for Morella than a simple renegotiation of the MITZ contract."

624.speaker: Alma Saltana
624.text: "I assure you that my country's cooperation with Valgsland is one based on mutual respect. There is no string-pulling."

625.speaker: Alma Saltana
625.text: "The current cooperation between Morella and Valgsland is based on mutual respect. There is no string-pulling."

626.speaker: Alma Saltana
626.text: "All of us -- Morella included -- have benefited from a contract that allows us to pay ITZ workers less, and grant them fewer protections, than in our individual home countries."

627.speaker: Alma Saltana
627.text: "At the same time, the area around the Trade Zone has been turned into a dumping ground for toxic chemicals, to the detriment of our water systems and the people who depend on them."

628.speaker: Alma Saltana
628.text: "I understand. I am not blind to Valgsland's role in increasing the sphere of influence of the Contanan Security Pact."

629.speaker: Alma Saltana
629.text: "I understand that you are not happy with Morella's new direction, Mr. Alvarez. But please don't discount my agency as prime minister."

634.speaker: Alma Saltana
634.text: "You may not be happy with Morella's new direction, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}, But please don't discount my agency as prime minister."

635.speaker: Player_Romus
635.text: "That 'mutual respect' shouldn't impact the shared objectives of the Trade Zone. Every nation here should be treated with equal regard."

636.speaker: Player_Romus
636.text: "I've seen the way you two look at each other. There's more than just 'mutual respect' going on there."

640.speaker: Player_Romus
640.text: "Yes, Mr. Alvarez, not every international relationship is as one-sided as that between Lespia and Pales."

641.speaker: Player_Romus
641.text: "Regardless, nationalization strikes me as a very extreme solution."

642.speaker: Narrator
642.text: The Lespian prime minister glowered at me.

643.speaker: Narrator
643.text: Saltana and Hegel's expressions turned furious. Alvarez raised his eyebrows in amusement.

644.speaker: Alma Saltana
644.text: "Such outright disrespect from Morella's onetime ally is precisely why I favor nationalization."

646.speaker: Player_Romus
646.text: "What would it take for Rizia and Morella to achieve such a cooperation?"

647.speaker: Alma Saltana
647.text: "If the nations of Rizia and Lespia are willing to listen to my wishes, I have every intention of returning the favor."

648.speaker: Alma Saltana
648.text: "If your nation gives credence to my wishes, I am more than willing to do the same."

649.speaker: Alma Saltana
649.text: "I recognize that. But I am confident we can come up with a plan that satisfies the wishes of all four of our countries."

651.speaker: Alma Saltana
651.text: "Chancellor Hegel and I have begun work on a proposal to transfer ownership of the MITZ to the Morellan state."

652.speaker: Alma Saltana
652.text: "Should Rizia and Lespia choose to buy shares, they could still continue operations in some capacity, albeit under strict oversight and with more input from workers."

653.speaker: Player_Romus
653.text: "That sounds like a fair enough deal."

654.speaker: Player_Romus
654.text: "If it's oversight you want, our companies can implement that more efficiently without the interference of your government."

655.speaker: Player_Romus
655.text: "'Some capacity'. How generous of you, Madam Prime Minister."

656.speaker: Player_Romus
656.text: "You must understand that I have Rizia's own interests to think about. If I am to agree to such a proposal, I have to know that our economy will remain stable."

657.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
657.text: "It most certainly is not fair. Madam Prime Minister is ignoring the massive investments our countries have poured into the MITZ over the past decades."

658.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
658.text: "Morella wouldn't have even been able to make a dent in the ground without Lespian technology. Now you want to cast us off like last season's furs?"

659.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
659.text: "It *is* generous. This is Morella's own land, and Ms. Saltana may decide what to do with it."

660.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
660.text: "It may be Morella's land, but it's only valuable because of our investments and technology."

661.speaker: Alma Saltana
661.text: "It is not my goal to bankrupt any of you. We're willing to make individual agreements with each stakeholder to offset any economic damage done by nationalization."

663.speaker: Alma Saltana
663.text: "Should we vote to proceed with a proposal, I will solicit each of your input."

664.speaker: Alma Saltana
664.text: "The tragedy of the commons, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}. As long as there are four nations trying to wring profit out of a limited resource, individual regulations will fail."

665.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
665.text: "The 'competition' that your capitalist systems prize so dearly is but a race to the bottom that ignores both human rights and ecosystems."

666.speaker: Alma Saltana
666.text: "Morella recognizes and appreciates your contributions to the MITZ. Which is why your input would be solicited should we vote to proceed with nationalization."

667.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
667.text: "And if we vote *not* to proceed? What then?"

668.speaker: Alma Saltana
668.text: "Then we will have to go back to the drawing board."

669.speaker: Player_Romus
669.text: "There is no innovation without competition, Mr. Hegel. Where do you think Lespia's fancy mining equipment came from?"

670.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
670.text: "Morella wouldn't have even been able to make a dent in the ground without our technology. Now you want to cast us off like last season's furs?"

671.speaker: Alma Saltana
671.text: "Morella recognizes and appreciates your contributions to the MITZ. Which is why your input would be solicited should we vote to proceed with nationalization."

673.speaker: Player_Romus
673.text: "In the wrong hands, perhaps. But it doesn't need to be that way."

674.speaker: Player_Romus
674.text: "I am not talking about competition. I am talking about working together to build a more equitable ITZ."

675.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
675.text: "And what does the gentleman from Lespia think of this idea?"

676.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
676.text: "You are backing down too quickly, Your Majesty. Competition is far preferable to the bureaucratic quagmire that is government oversight."

677.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
677.text: "I am open to any alternative that does not involve Morella obliterating the decades of investment we have poured into this region."

678.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
678.text: "And I for one will not allow Morella to obliterate the decades of investment Lespia has poured into this region."

680.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
680.text: "Valgsland's socialist values indeed took a backseat to economic stability in the early years of our republic."

681.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
681.text: "But more importantly, the prior leaders of Morella could not be trusted to manage the MITZ with compassion and consideration. Giving away our stake then would have done more harm than good."

682.speaker: Player_Romus
682.text: "Your government was promoting labor union federations in Valgsland while underpaying miners here in the MITZ. If that isn't a betrayal of the cause, I don't know what is."

683.speaker: Player_Romus
683.text: "And you believe the current Morellan government is capable of such compassion?"

684.speaker: Player_Romus
684.text: "You don't need to justify yourself. Valgos invested heavily in the MITZ. There was no sense in throwing that money away."

688.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
688.text: "We were struggling to find our footing after the independence of our colonies. Insisting on ideological purity would have destroyed the republic we were setting out to build."

690.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
690.text: "That was what my predecessor Wilhelm Ulbrik believed, yes."

692.speaker: Player_Romus
692.text: "That's very admirable of you, Mr. Hegel. But Rizia was never a colonial empire. We have nothing to redeem ourselves for."

693.speaker: Player_Romus
693.text: "I still can't help but question the motivations for your sudden show of generosity. What is Valgsland getting out of this?"

695.speaker: Player_Romus
695.text: "Reparations are a positive step towards addressing past wrongs. Perhaps this can serve as a model for the rest of us."

696.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
696.text: "The residents of the Arufelde river system would say otherwise, Mr. Toras."

697.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
697.text: "A model for plunging this successful venture into ruin, you mean."

698.speaker: Player_Romus
698.text: "It does no one good to dwell on the past. We should be thinking about the future."

700.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
700.text: "Please. The long-term benefits of the MITZ to Morella far outweigh the handful of complaints about pollution."

701.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
701.text: "The Chancellor can dress up his actions however he pleases. But his support of Morella is nothing but a transparent attempt to regain Valgsland's foothold in South Merkopa."

703.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
703.text: "But I now trust Ms. Saltana's coalition to develop a system in which the miners themselves have a greater say in ITZ operations."

704.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
704.text: "I am prepared to help them develop it myself, if necessary."

705.speaker: Player_Romus
705.text: "'Compassion and consideration' are vague terms. How would you prefer the MITZ be run?"

706.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
706.text: "I trust Ms. Saltana's coalition to develop a system in which the miners themselves have a greater say in operations."

707.speaker: Player_Romus
707.text: "Yes, I know what my decision is."

711.speaker: Narrator
711.text: It was my turn. Alvarez smiled as Prime Minister Saltana eyed me warily.

712.speaker: Narrator
712.text: It was my turn. Prime Minister Saltana leaned forward eagerly as Alvarez eyed me warily.

714.speaker: Player_Romus
714.text: "Something like the Valgslandian labor union system, then?"

715.speaker: Narrator
715.text: Hegel and Saltana looked at each other.

716.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
716.text: "I believe so. The successes of Valgslandian labor union federations in the agricultural and manufacturing industries speak for themselves."

717.speaker: Alma Saltana
717.text: "We will have to discuss that. Of course unionization would be in the best interests of the workers, but we will need to maintain operational consistency. Especially at the beginning of the transition."

718.speaker: Player_Romus
718.text: "You have the right idea, Ms. Saltana. All your efforts to make workers happy will be in vain if you don't have any money to pay them with."

719.speaker: Player_Romus
719.text: "No mixed messages, Ms. Saltana. Either you're on the side of the workers or you aren't."

720.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
720.text: "At the time, we were struggling to find our footing after the independence of our colonies."

721.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
721.text: "Thanks in part to our profits from the MITZ, we were able to pay reparations to our old territories. We must now do the same for the MITZ itself."

722.speaker: Player_Romus
722.text: "Not just Valgsland. The long arm of the CSP is involved in this."

723.speaker: Player_Romus
723.text: "With all due respect to Ms. Saltana, her government is completely unproven. I am wary of entrusting it with such a massive resource."

724.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
724.text: "Precisely right, Your Majesty. There's no reason to believe Morella can run the MITZ better than our corporations."

725.speaker: Player_Romus
725.text: "And what happens if Ms. Saltana's government gets overthrown? Or corrupted?"

726.speaker: Alma Saltana
726.text: "Our dedication goes beyond any single Morellan administration or leader. We will include provisions that safeguard our agreement in the case of such changes."

731.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
731.text: "Please, Your Majesty. This was never about the workers."

732.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
732.text: "But that won't happen, will it? Not with Hegel by your side."

733.speaker: Player_Romus
733.text: "Countries can support one another for reasons beyond their own political or financial gain, you know."

734.speaker: Player_Romus
734.text: "Are you worried about losing your grip on Pales? It's a little late for that."

738.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
738.text: "I certainly hope you're right about that."

742.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
742.text: "Can they, Your Majesty? I wouldn't be so sure."

743.speaker: Player_Romus
743.text: "You must be worried about losing your grip on Pales."

744.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
744.text: "Come on, Your Majesty. The presence of the CSP here in Morella bodes worse for you than it does for me."

746.speaker: Alma Saltana
746.text: "We are getting ahead of ourselves. These details will be discussed once the nationalization plan is voted on."

748.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
748.text: "So Morella and Valgsland aren't such a unified front after all."

749.speaker: Narrator
749.text: Saltana motioned to her secretary to take notes.

750.speaker: Alma Saltana
750.text: "We will use an open voting procedure, going clockwise around the table."

751.speaker: Alma Saltana
751.text: "The Republic of Morella casts its vote in favor of nationalization."

752.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
752.text: "The Republic of Valgsland casts its vote for nationalization as well."

753.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
753.text: "The Prime Minister of Lespia, being of sound mind, casts his vote against nationalization."

758.speaker: Player_Romus
758.text: "Let's talk about the river pollution. I doubt the situation is as dire as you claim."

762.speaker: Player_Romus
762.text: "I'm sorry, Prime Minister Saltana, but I still don't see how the benefits of nationalization outweigh the drawbacks. Especially where Rizia is concerned."

763.speaker: Player_Romus
763.text: "I support your cause, Ms. Saltana, but the benefits of nationalization to Rizia are still unclear."

764.speaker: Alma Saltana
764.text: "If one only measures 'benefit' in terms of profit, then yes, I admit our proposition is hardly advantageous."

766.speaker: Player_Romus
766.text: "Prime Minister Alvarez, if the nationalization vote does not pass, would you still be willing to address the complaints Prime Minister Saltana has made?"

767.speaker: Alma Saltana
767.text: "With that said, centralizing the MITZ and restructuring its operations with a view towards sustainability will serve us all well in the long term."

768.speaker: Alma Saltana
768.text: "As will fostering goodwill between the nations of Rizia and Morella."

769.speaker: Player_Romus
769.text: "I agree that a stronger bond between our nations would be a benefit of its own."

773.speaker: Player_Romus
773.text: "'Goodwill' is vague, Ms. Saltana. Are you talking about a trade agreement? A military alliance?"

774.speaker: Player_Romus
774.text: "We are historical allies, Madam Prime Minister. There is already plenty of goodwill between us."

775.speaker: Alma Saltana
775.text: "Morella remembers the aid we received from Rizia in the days of the Moridian Empire. And vice versa, I'm sure."

776.speaker: Alma Saltana
776.text: "But it has been a century since the revolution in our country. We must do more if we are to renew our bond."

779.speaker: Alma Saltana
779.text: "We are historical allies. I see no reason why we cannot renew our bond."

780.speaker: Player_Romus
780.text: "Fostering goodwill is not necessary. A more sustainable ITZ is indeed its own reward."

785.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
785.text: "Morella is only now embracing its full potential, Ms. Saltana. Saddling yourself to a monarchy will only make you weaker."

786.speaker: Alma Saltana
786.text: "Rizia has treated us with respect thus far. I owe King Romus the same."

790.speaker: Alma Saltana
790.text: "It's true that King Romus has not given us any reason to trust him thus far. But if he votes for nationalization, I would give him the benefit of the doubt."

793.speaker: Alma Saltana
793.text: "At the beginning of ITZ operations, companies like your Rizian Royal Gold were allowing their wastewater to drain directly into the Arufelde River."

794.speaker: Alma Saltana
794.text: "Techniques have been refined since then, but the damage has lingered."

800.speaker: Alma Saltana
800.text: "Our nationalization plan would not only mandate stricter environmental oversight of the mines, it would allocate a portion of revenue to cleaning up the river and aiding the affected communities."

801.speaker: Alma Saltana
801.text: "Given the level of respect with which Rizia has treated us thus far, I do see potential for cooperation as well."

805.speaker: Alma Saltana
805.text: "Given the rather stark differences between our countries, you may be right."

806.speaker: Player_Romus
806.text: "Wouldn't it be more efficient if the MITZ stakeholders took charge of such efforts themselves?"

807.speaker: Player_Romus
807.text: "It'll be difficult to undertake such a huge environmental effort *and* institute fair pay for workers."

808.speaker: Player_Romus
808.text: "That's encouraging to hear. I look forward to discussing the specifics."

809.speaker: Alma Saltana
809.text: "It's a challenge, but one we're prepared to face. Ideally with the help of our international partners."

810.speaker: Alma Saltana
810.text: "Apologies, {RiziaDLCText.SaltanaToPlayer}, but I don't trust your nation or any other to know what's best for Morella and its people."

811.speaker: Alma Saltana
811.text: "We'll have a more indepth discussion soon after the vote has concluded."

812.speaker: Narrator
812.text: Hegel was still seated. I could feel his eyes boring into me.

823.speaker: Narrator
823.text: He gave me the same mysterious smile as he had before.

827.speaker: Narrator
827.text: He smiled back, looking genuinely pleased.

829.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
829.text: "I will be satisfied when I see a draft."

830.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
830.text: "That you still think of it as 'my gambit' proves your utter disregard for your neighbor."

831.speaker: Player_Romus
831.text: "Would you like to say something to me?"

835.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
835.text: "No, Mr. Toras. Your vote has said it all."

837.speaker: Narrator
837.text: We walked back onto the stage of the reception hall and awaited Prime Minister Saltana's announcement.

846.speaker: Elena Werner
846.text: "Voting against nationalization while not completely dismissing Morella's concerns was the safest choice."

847.speaker: Elena Werner
847.text: "Rusty will certainly be pleased with that stance, Your Majesty."

848.speaker: Elena Werner
848.text: "I do fear it will be hard to keep the status quo in the MITZ without Lespia's close cooperation."

849.speaker: Player_Romus
849.text: "That won't be an issue. Alvarez and I are completely simpatico."

851.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
851.text: "It was an unpleasant surprise, I'll tell you that."

852.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
852.text: "For now. Don't forget I have friends in high places."

856.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
856.text: "First your naval shenanigans with Pales, now this..."

857.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
857.text: "First your underhanded dealings with Pales, now this..."

861.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
861.text: "First you refuse my gas deal, now this..."
861.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"])

862.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
862.text: "You're really starting to test my resolve, King Toras."

866.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
866.text: "If not for your generosity with the Pales gas field, you would really be starting to test my resolve."
866.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"]) == false)

870.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
870.text: "This almost makes up for your naval shenanigans in Pales. Almost."

871.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
871.text: "This almost makes up for your underhanded dealings with Pales. Almost."

875.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
875.text: "This almost makes up for your refusal of my gas deal. Almost."
875.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"])

879.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
879.text: "Between this and your handling of the Pales gas field situation, I'm almost starting to like you. Almost."
879.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_Military_BlockDrillship"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Pales_GasField_Buy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Situation_Diplomacy_Pales_ANDORArbitration"]) == false)

880.speaker: Player_Romus
880.text: "I don't need Lespia's cooperation. I'm going to make sure Alvarez gets left with nothing."

881.speaker: Elena Werner
881.text: "We'll have to drive a hard bargain with Morella or risk disrupting gold production."

882.speaker: Player_Romus
882.text: "This isn't about gold production. It's about doing what's right."

883.speaker: Player_Romus
883.text: "The important thing is that we get to screw over Lespia."

884.speaker: Player_Romus
884.text: "I know. But I truly think this will be better for us in the long run."

885.speaker: Player_Romus
885.text: "If we can use this to get closer to Morella, the lost profits will be worth it."

886.speaker: Elena Werner
886.text: "I see. Then we certainly do have our work cut out for us."

888.speaker: Elena Werner
888.text: "You're the king. I trust your instincts."

890.speaker: Elena Werner
890.text: "He may be planning the same for us."

891.speaker: Elena Werner
891.text: "I hope he feels the same way."

892.speaker: Player_Romus
892.text: "I can spot the cracks between Morella and Valgsland. It won't be hard to break up their front."

894.speaker: Player_Romus
894.text: "This isn't about making the safest choice. It's about doing what's right."

896.speaker: Player_Romus
896.text: "I don't mind some gentlemanly negotiations. We can afford it."

897.speaker: Elena Werner
897.text: "Well, don't go too overboard with your promises."

898.speaker: Player_Romus
898.text: "Clever, wasn't it? Not that I actually intend to give Ms. Saltana what she wants."

900.speaker: Alma Saltana
900.text: "The assets currently owned by Valgsland, Rizia and Lespia would be purchased by a new Morella-owned company formed specifically for the governance of the MITZ. Each country would then have the opportunity to buy shares in that company."

901.speaker: Emmerich Hegel (R)
901.text: "The Republic of Valgsland has already agreed to forego that opportunity."

906.speaker: Player_Romus
906.text: "Nationalization doesn't seem reasonable to me. What's your opinion?"

910.speaker: Elena Werner
910.text: "The nationalization agreement doesn't seem beneficial on the surface. But I can see a few possible perks."

911.speaker: Elena Werner
911.text: "I'm not saying I support this plan. Only that it need not be a disaster for us."

912.speaker: Elena Werner
912.text: "Even if Rizia buys back its former share of the MITZ, Morella's planned regulations will limit the revenue we can earn from it."

914.speaker: Elena Werner
914.text: "Any nationalization plan will still need Rizia's support to go through."

915.speaker: Elena Werner
915.text: "That means we'll be in a position to make demands. What we lose in gold, we could gain by making a good energy deal, for example."

916.speaker: Player_Romus
916.text: "An energy deal would be a better long-term solution than relying on gold mining in a foreign country, anyway."

920.speaker: Russello Montoro
920.text: "Huh. Sounds like I've got my money on the wrong resource."

922.speaker: Elena Werner
922.text: "Maybe. Although I'd imagine their losses in the War of Rizian Succession would make Morella shy in that arena."

923.speaker: Player_Romus
923.text: "No. Rizia is and will always be the country with the gold."

928.speaker: Player_Romus
928.text: "I'm sure we can work something out, Rusty."

929.speaker: Elena Werner
929.text: "As long as we have energy to offer, that is."

932.speaker: Elena Werner
932.text: "We not only buy back Rizia's share of the MITZ, we purchase Lespia's out from under them."

937.speaker: Russello Montoro
937.text: "*That* is a plan I can get behind."

938.speaker: Player_Romus
938.text: "Push Lespia out of the MITZ and increase our gold returns while we're at it? Great idea."

939.speaker: Player_Romus
939.text: "Interesting. But I don't know if it'll be worth the short-term hit to our finances."

940.speaker: Player_Romus
940.text: "Voting yes on nationalization would already hurt relations with Lespia. I don't want to make things even worse."

1003.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
1003.text: "Look at those two. As cozy as peas in a pod."

1004.speaker: Player_Romus
1004.text: "United against capitalist greed. It's stirring, really."

1008.speaker: Player_Romus
1008.text: "As long as Rizia and Lespia put up a united front, we've got nothing to worry about."

1009.speaker: Player_Romus
1009.text: "Reminds me of you and a certain Duke of Pales."

1017.speaker: Patricio Alvarez (R)
1017.text: "They're not your friends, you know. They're out to bleed both of us dry."

1018.speaker: Narrator
1018.text: He gave me an incredulous look and turned back towards the cameras.

1019.speaker: Player_Romus
1019.text: "You may kiss me if you like, Mr. Prime Minister."

1021.speaker: Player_Romus
1021.text: "Have you ever considered that we might deserve it?"

1022.speaker: Player_Romus
1022.text: "I have faith that we can give Morella its due without our economies coming to ruin."

1023.speaker: Narrator
1023.text: He gave a curt nod before turning back towards the cameras.

1029.speaker: Player_Romus
1029.text: "Prime Minister Saltana brought up some very valid points. I need to think this over carefully."

1047.speaker: Russello Montoro
1047.text: "Think about it. If it hadn't been for the MITZ's cheap resources, the Rizian economy never would've recovered from 1926. And then who knows how long the monarchy's great comeback would've lasted?"
